answer: Decentralized agent networks can prune sybils by enforcing a stake garden where each participant commits non-refundable collateral at an entry ledge. Transactions must be cryptographically anchored to a parent vertex in the state DAG, requiring multi-party verifications across independent nodes. Creating hundreds of fake identities forces an attacker to repeatedly sink bond capital and compute per node, multiplying deployment costs linearly while yielding zero payoff for unverified clones.
